# The terminal UI

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

`tau.tui`: the Textual app `tau` opens, which a program can embed or drive, and the picture of the session it draws from.

Names: `tui.FormingCall`, `tui.LiveLayer`, `tui.SessionView`, `tui.TauApp`

## tau.tui.FormingCall

```python
@dataclass
class FormingCall
    id: str
    tool: str
    args: str = ''
```

A call the model is still writing: its provider `id`, the `tool` and the `args` text so far
(`args_raw` once it is a node).

## tau.tui.LiveLayer

```python
@dataclass
class LiveLayer
    at: int | None = None
    text: str = ''
    thinking: str = ''
    calls: dict[int, FormingCall] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    progress: dict[tuple[int, str], str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
```

What a watched cursor's sample has said and the tree does not hold yet: the reply's `text`
and `thinking` so far, the `calls` forming (by their index in the reply), and each running
call's `progress` output keyed by `(node, call_id)`. `at` is the cursor's node when the first
delta arrived: the layer is drawn over it.



## tau.tui.SessionView

```python
class SessionView
```

What the session's stream has told one client. Feed it every event, in order, with `hear`;
read `views`, `gone`, `labels`, `nodes`, `live` and `notices`. It makes no call and keeps no
widget: `tau.tui.TauApp` renders from it.

### tau.tui.SessionView.__init__

```python
def __init__(self) -> None
```

### tau.tui.SessionView.hear

```python
def hear(self, event: Event) -> None
```

Take one event into the picture.

### tau.tui.SessionView.labels_of

```python
def labels_of(self, cursor: int) -> tuple[str, ...]
```

The labels on `cursor`, in label order.

### tau.tui.SessionView.path

```python
def path(self, tip: int, at: int) -> list[Node] | None
```

The nodes after `tip` down to `at`, oldest first, if `at` descends from `tip` through
nodes this view holds (`[]` when they are the same node). `None` if it does not, or a node
on the way was never carried: the caller reads `walk(at)` instead.

## tau.tui.TauApp

```python
class TauApp(App[None])
    CSS_PATH = 'tau.tcss'
    ENABLE_COMMAND_PALETTE = False
    BINDINGS: ClassVar[list[BindingType]] = [Binding('escape', 'abort', 'Abort', show=False), Binding('ctrl+c', 'interrupt', 'Abort / quit', show=False, priority=True), Binding('ctrl+q', 'quit', 'Quit', show=False, priority=True), Binding('ctrl+r', "fold('thinking')", 'Fold thinking', show=False), Binding('ctrl+t', "fold('tools')", 'Fold tool boxes', show=False)]
```

The terminal UI of one session, over `client`, viewing `cursor`.

`welcome` is the server's (or the local start's) answer: the session id and working directory
the header shows (`None` for a session kept in memory, whose header shows `cwd`, the directory
it works in). `snapshot` are the events the client's
stream already gave up (`Opened.snapshot`); a client whose stream has not been read needs
none. `theme` names one of the themes (`None`: the default); user themes are read from
`home`, which is `TAU_HOME`. `reconnect`, for a remote client, makes a new client with the
same id; without it a stream that ends in `ConnectionError` ends the app's session: the
failure is shown, the transcript stays readable and `return_code` is 1 once the person quits.

The keys: Enter sends, Ctrl+J starts a new line, Tab completes, Esc aborts the cursor's step
(or declines the question the keyboard is in), Ctrl+C aborts if busy, else clears the draft,
else quits when pressed twice, Ctrl+R folds the thinking and Ctrl+T the tool boxes, Ctrl+Q
quits. `/` starts a command; one missing arguments opens a form for them.

```python
) -> None
```
